overall: Board violated the OML by holding five executive sessions discussing complaints against individuals without giving them Purpose 1 notice and rights; remedial steps were appropriate; compliance and training ordered.

allegations.summary: Board met in executive session on five dates to discuss complaints against individuals without notifying them or giving them Purpose 1 rights (presence, counsel, speaking, recording).
allegations.key_passage: The Personnel Board repeatedly violated the Open Meeting Law by entering executive session to discuss complaints against individuals

allegations.summary: Complainant's concern that he was not given notice or a chance to attend, bring counsel, or record executive sessions discussing him is tied to the Purpose 1 rights the Board failed to provide.
allegations.key_passage: If a public body enters executive session for Purpose 1, it must notify the individual who is the subject of the discussion in writing at least 48 hours before the meeting and afford the individual certain rights

allegations.summary: Complainant objected that the Board's remedial steps (acknowledgment, apology, nullification) were insufficient, and that other former members had not apologized.
allegations.key_passage: The remedial steps taken by the new Board in response to the complaint were appropriate given the seriousness of the violations.

allegations.summary: Complainant wanted the Board's apology to be judged sufficient and the content of the apology reviewed.
allegations.key_passage: generally will not take a position on whether the manner or content of the apology was sufficient

allegations.summary: Complainant asked that complaints against him on file with the Town Human Resources Department be dropped or acted upon.
allegations.key_passage: we have no authority to order the Town to take action as our authority extends only to the public body

allegations.summary: Complainant sought unredacted copies of complaints and documents used in the executive sessions discussing him.
allegations.key_passage: We make no finding with respect to whether the documents Mr. Philpot seeks have been properly withheld or redacted under the Public Records Law.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law
Attend an Open Meeting Law training within sixty (60) days of receipt of the letter and certify completion to the Attorney General
Publicly release the executive session minutes and documents used in the five illegal sessions, subject to privilege and Public Records Law exemptions
remedy_passage: we order the Board's immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
